llm.summary: This appears to be a legitimate local memory/context pipeline, but it should be reviewed because it can make persistent workspace changes and turn memory retrieval into default agent behavior.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the artifacts: routing user messages, retrieving local memory snippets, compressing context, validating fixtures, and installing a context_pipeline bundle.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The apply flow directs agents to install files, patch AGENTS.md, run validation/watchdog scripts, and make the pipeline default behavior, without a clear pre-write confirmation boundary.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The installer is a straightforward local copy from bundled assets and the validator checks hashes/schemas; setup commands are disclosed, but they still modify the workspace and inspect git state.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime retrieval is scoped to memory files, but those files can include daily logs, people/account notes, ops notes, and other private workspace context that may be pulled into future prompts.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill creates/updates context_pipeline, patches AGENTS.md, writes debug/audit artifacts, and has a memory commit workflow that appends persistent notes from broad natural-language triggers.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want this skill to modify the workspace and make local memory retrieval part of normal agent behavior. Review the AGENTS.md patch, context_pipeline files, memory commit workflow, and debug/audit artifact paths before enabling it, and avoid storing secrets or sensitive account details in memory files that the pipeline may retrieve.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: File reads and writes are expected for this skill, but the artifacts do not define a clear permission boundary beyond naming paths like AGENTS.md, context_pipeline, and memory files.
[SDI-2] expected: The setup commands are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but they go beyond prompt configuration by modifying files and exposing command/git output.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad router and activation phrases mainly create reliability and unintended-activation risk; the behavior is not hidden, but it can steer default memory retrieval unexpectedly.
[SQP-2] expected: Workspace writes, AGENTS.md patching, runtime artifact persistence, and memory appends are central to the skill, but the artifacts lack an explicit consent/dry-run step before persistent changes.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry is clean, and static scan metadata reports no suspicious patterns; this lowers malware concern but does not remove the local persistence and default-behavior review concerns.
